[[File:Small rhombihexacron.stl|thumb|3D model of a small rhombihexacron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''small rhombihexacron''' (or '''small dipteral disdodecahedron''') is the dual of the [[small rhombihexahedron]]. It is visually identical to the [[small hexacronic icositetrahedron]]. Its faces are [[antiparallelogram]]s formed by pairs of [[coplanar]] [[triangle]]s.

== Proportions==
Each antiparallelogram has two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2})\approx 16.842\,116\,236\,30^{\circ}</math> and two angles of <math>\arccos(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2})\approx 98.421\,058\,118\,15^{\circ}</math>. The diagonals of each antiparallelogram  intersect at an angle of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{2})\approx 64.736\,825\,645\,55^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\frac{-7-4\sqrt{2}}{17})\approx 138.117\,959\,055\,51^{\circ}</math>. The ratio between the lengths of the long edges and the short ones equals <math>\sqrt{2}</math>.
